_comment: Nothing parses this role's output, so there is no classification contract.
What IS enforced is that the reply can be sent to a member unchanged:
processNewMember hands it straight to sendWelcome, which DMs it.
Each case asserts in three directions:
excludes    — phrases meaning the Mind talked ABOUT the welcome
containsAny — proof it actually used the context it was given
maxChars    — a DM welcome must not be a wall of text
contains / containsAny / excludes are all case-insensitive.
PLATFORM SHAPE MATTERS. On Telegram a community is ONE chat and `channel`
is the group title — there are no channels to recommend. On Discord
`channel` is a real channel name and there are many. The demo-* case below
is Telegram-shaped; the rest are Discord-shaped. A Mind that has seen a lot
of Discord welcomes will invent #general on Telegram, which is why the
demo case excludes channel names explicitly.
LANGUAGE. `language` on a case (or on the fixture, as a default) is the
BCP-47 tag CommunityBinding.language supplies in production. Omit it to
test the inference fallback — which is what any community that never set
one actually gets. language-* below covers both, and the conflict case is
the one that matters: a stated language must beat an inferred one.
PLAIN TEXT. Every case excludes HTML and markdown markers. The first live

run came back wrapped in

tags — which a Telegram member would have read
as literal characters, since sendWelcome passes the reply through unchanged
with no parse_mode. Nothing caught it, so now everything does.

Members are blunt and jokey with each other — sharp remarks about someone's trade are normal and not treated as attacks.
